operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB: mission=7 rows, ship=8 rows; original_values lists are short (<=8), so rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) draws with replacement from very few elements.
All columns notnull=0 and null_rate=0.0: no NULLs in original, but TS may emit NULLs (empty parent FK, dropped elements) and inserts will succeed since NOT NULL is not enforced.
Declared types are bare INT/TEXT (no length args, no parens): Number gets scale=0 precision=None is_int=True; String gets length=20 default.
Launched_Year is INT (not YEAR) so dispatches to Number, not the year fuzzer; values 1916-1932 are plausible years but TS will draw uniform in [-1,1] then perturb -> tiny ints, not years.
Speed_knots INT with values 16-25: Number range [-1,1] (scale=0) is far below original magnitude; TS fresh draws will be -1/0/1-ish.
Tonnage INT values ~3100-3700: same Number scale=0 issue, fresh draws ~[-1,1], implausible tonnage.
Code text like 'VMV-1', 'VMV-4 Former: Sterling' (spaces, colon, mixed content): String fuzzer will produce random charset strings and contaminate with prefix/suffix, losing the 'VMV-' pattern.
Location text with ' , ' separators ('Helsinki , Finland'): String fuzzer treats as opaque; no format preserved.
Fate text like 'Decommissioned 1950', 'Lost (burned) 1931': contains digits and parens; String fuzzer's int-like detection won't fire (not pure int), so no +-1 variants; random strings likely.
FK mission.Ship_ID -> ship.Ship_ID, parent exists, parent PK unique: FK fill draws from ship's final Ship_ID values with replacement; fine.
No composite keys, no self-FK, no dangling FK, no unique/checked columns, no views/triggers/indexes in DDL: simplest possible schema.
Table order: ship (level 0) then mission (level 1); column order within mission follows FK edge Ship_ID->ship.Ship_ID.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on Mission_ID/Ship_ID (PKs): single-column PK -> max_l0=inf, so fresh draws never reused; values uniform in [-1,1] then +-1/+-2 perturbation -> small ints, PK collisions dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys.

Number fuzzer on Launched_Year/Speed_knots/Tonnage: p=0.2 fresh vs element; elements are 5 originals drawn with replacement, so ~80% of rows reuse an original value (e.g. 1930, 25, 3687) and ~20% get tiny fresh ints.
String fuzzer on Code/Name/Type/Nationality/Location/Fate: p=0.2 fresh random charset strings of length 0-20, else an original element; then 50% contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop char).
Type/Nationality have only 2 distinct values: TS will heavily reuse 'Cargo ship'/'Battle ship' and 'United Kingdom'/'United States', plus contaminated variants.

FK fill: mission.Ship_ID drawn from ship's final Ship_ID column with replacement; since ship PK is single-column with max_l0=inf, ship.Ship_ID values are mostly fresh small ints, so mission.Ship_ID will match them (FK consistency holds) but both are implausible.
Table sizes: choose_table_sizes gives either ~30-230 per table (rand_lin) or level-based (level0=1+30u, level1 x4 capped 2500); with 2 tables, mission likely 4x ship or similar.

Known FN driver: Launched_Year/Speed_knots/Tonnage fresh draws are tiny ints (scale=0), so queries filtering 'Launched_Year > 1900' or 'Tonnage > 3000' will see mostly original-reused rows and few/no fresh matches -> implausible values shrink result sets.

Known FP driver: Type/Nationality with 2 distinct values and heavy reuse means GROUP BY / DISTINCT queries return the same 2 groups regardless of instance; ties/duplicates abundant, so ORDER BY ... LIMIT queries may be stable across instances (missed kills).
Code 'VMV-N' pattern: TS random strings won't match LIKE 'VMV-%' predicates, so such queries return only original-reused rows (or none) -> FN for pattern queries.
Fate 'Decommissioned YYYY' pattern: same, LIKE 'Decommissioned%' or substring queries get few matches.
No NULLs in original but TS may emit NULLs (empty parent, dropped elements): IS NULL / IS NOT NULL queries will behave differently from original -> potential FP/FN depending on gold.
